What is BDIX and Why Does It Matter?

BDIX (Bangladesh Internet Exchange) is a local peering point that allows ISPs to exchange traffic domestically. This means when you download from a BDIX-connected FTP server, you get blazing fast speeds — sometimes 10–50x faster than your international download speed. All major Mirpur ISPs support BDIX.

posts.title: Why Is My Internet Slow in Mirpur? (10 Causes & Fixes)
posts.metaDescription: Is your internet slow in Mirpur? Discover the 10 most common causes and practical fixes to speed up your connection in Mirpur, Dhaka.

content.text: 10 Reasons Your Internet Is Slow in Mirpur

items: Peak hour congestion (6–11 PM) — Most ISPs in Mirpur experience heavy congestion on weekday evenings. Try scheduling large downloads for after midnight.
Wi-Fi interference — Walls, microwave ovens, and neighboring networks can cut your Wi-Fi speed by 50%. Use 5GHz band or Ethernet cable.
Old router — Routers over 3 years old may not support modern speeds. Upgrade to a Wi-Fi 6 router for best performance.
ISP throttling — Some ISPs slow your connection after you've used a certain amount of data. Check your plan's fair usage policy.
Shared bandwidth — Cable internet is shared with your neighborhood. Fiber connections are less affected.
DNS slowness — Your ISP's default DNS servers may be slow. Switch to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Google (8.8.8.8) for faster browsing.
Malware — Background malware can consume your bandwidth. Run an antivirus scan.
Too many devices — 5+ connected devices sharing a 10 Mbps plan will feel slow for everyone.
Faulty cable — Physical damage to coaxial or ethernet cable causes speed drops. Inspect your cable runs.
ISP technical issues — Check Speed Pro's outage reporter to see if others in your area are affected.

items.q: How do I report a slow connection to my ISP?
items.a: Screenshot your Speed Pro results showing the slow speed, then contact your ISP's customer support. If unresolved, file a complaint at BTRC: 16996.

posts.title: The History of Internet in Mirpur, Dhaka — From Dial-Up to Fiber
posts.metaDescription: The fascinating history of internet connectivity in Mirpur, Dhaka — from dial-up modems in the 2000s to the fiber revolution of 2025.

content.text: In the early 2000s, internet access in Mirpur was limited to dial-up connections through BTTB (now Teletalk). Speeds were measured in Kbps, and connection costs were charged per minute. A family would pay ৳2,000+ per month for just a few hours of internet.

ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line) arrived in Mirpur through BTTB and early ISPs like Link3 Technologies. Suddenly, always-on connections at 512 Kbps to 2 Mbps were possible. Cyber cafes boomed during this period.

Local ISPs began laying cable networks across Mirpur's sections. MirpurNet, MNET, and dozens of smaller providers emerged, offering 5–20 Mbps for ৳400–৳800/month. BDIX was established, creating a local internet exchange that would transform content delivery.

BDIX-connected FTP servers proliferated, giving Mirpur users access to massive local content libraries. Downloading Bangla movies, software, and game patches at 50–100 Mbps became normal while international speeds were only 10–20 Mbps.

Fiber optic infrastructure reached most of Mirpur between 2023 and 2025. ISPs like BAS Network and Inspire Broadband began offering 100–200 Mbps fiber plans, and real-world speeds finally matched advertised speeds consistently.
